title: 割集电压方程的矩阵形式 Q·Y·Qᵀ·U_t = Q·I_s − Q·Y·U_s
statement: 电路如图（U_s1 = 12 V，I_s6 = 2 A，R_1 = 2 Ω，R_2 = 6 Ω，R_3 = 3 Ω，R_4 = 4 Ω，R_5 = 2 Ω，R_7 = 4 Ω）。U_s1 与 R_1 串联为支路 1，I_s6 单独为支路 6，其余每个电阻一条支路；结点 1、2、3、4（4 接地为参考结点），支路编号与方向见有向图。
标准支路（复合支路）约定：支路 k 的电压 U_k、电流 I_k 取支路方向（关联），I_k = Y_k(U_k + U_sk) − I_sk；U_sk 的“+”极在支路终点一侧（推动电流沿支路方向流动）时为正，I_sk 的方向与支路方向**相反**时为正。
选树 T = {1, 2, 5}，以树支电压 U_t = (U_1, U_2, U_5)ᵀ 为未知量（基本割集方向同树支方向）。基本割集矩阵为
写出 Y_t·U_t = J_t，其中 Y_t = Q_f·Y·Q_fᵀ，J_t = Q_f·I_s − Q_f·Y·U_s，求矩阵元素与树支电压。

questions.explain: 割集 1、2 共有支路 4、6、7，在两个割集中的方向都相同（都是 −1）：+(0.25 + 0 + 0.25) = 0.5 S。注意割集法的“互导”可以是正的。

questions.ask: 右端 J_t = Q_f·I_s − Q_f·Y·U_s 的第 1 个元素 = ?
解 Y_t·U_t = J_t，树支电压 U_t1 = U_1 = ?
结点 3 的电压 u_3 = ?（对结点 4）
questions.explain: 沿树从结点 3 走到结点 4：u_3 = U_5 + U_2 + U_1 的相反数？按定义 U_k = 起点电压 − 终点电压：u_4 − u_1 = U_1，u_1 − u_2 = U_2，u_2 − u_3 = U_5，相加得 u_4 − u_3 = U_1 + U_2 + U_5 = −7 V，所以 u_3 = 7 V。

hints: 支路导纳：Y = diag(1/2, 1/6, 1/3, 1/4, 1/2, 0, 1/4) S（电流源支路导纳为 0）；电源：U_s1 = 12 V、I_s6 = 2 A 的符号按标准支路约定。
Y_t 的元素可以“观察”出来：对角元 = 割集中所有支路导纳之和；非对角元 = 两割集共有支路的导纳，方向一致取正、相反取负。
解出树支电压后，任一结点电压可以沿树从参考结点累加得到。

en.title: Cut-set equations in matrix form Q·Y·Qᵀ·U_t = Q·I_s − Q·Y·U_s
statement: The circuit is drawn below (U_s1 = 12 V, I_s6 = 2 A, R_1 = 2 Ω, R_2 = 6 Ω, R_3 = 3 Ω, R_4 = 4 Ω, R_5 = 2 Ω, R_7 = 4 Ω). U_s1 in series with R_1 is branch 1, I_s6 alone is branch 6, and each other resistor is one branch; nodes 1, 2, 3, 4 (4 grounded, the reference), branch numbers and directions as in the graph.

Standard (composite) branch convention: U_k and I_k follow the branch direction (associated), I_k = Y_k(U_k + U_sk) − I_sk; U_sk is positive when its "+" is toward the end of the branch (it pushes current along the branch), and I_sk is positive when it points **against** the branch direction.
Choose the tree T = {1, 2, 5} and take the tree-branch voltages U_t = (U_1, U_2, U_5)ᵀ as unknowns (fundamental cut-sets directed like their tree branches). The fundamental cut-set matrix is
Write Y_t·U_t = J_t with Y_t = Q_f·Y·Q_fᵀ and J_t = Q_f·I_s − Q_f·Y·U_s, and find matrix entries and the tree-branch voltages.

questions.explain: Cut-set 1 (tree branch 1) contains branches 1, 4, 6, 7: 0.5 + 0.25 + 0 + 0.25 = 1 S (branch 6 is a current source, admittance 0).
Cut-sets 1 and 2 share branches 4, 6, 7, oriented the same way in both (−1 and −1): +(0.25 + 0 + 0.25) = 0.5 S. Mutual terms of the cut-set method can be positive.

questions.ask: Solve Y_t·U_t = J_t: tree-branch voltage U_t1 = U_1 = ?
questions.explain: U_t = (−9.25, 2.75, −0.5)ᵀ V. U_1 is measured from 4 to 1, so node 1 is at 9.25 V.
Walk the tree: by definition U_k = start voltage − end voltage, so u_4 − u_1 = U_1, u_1 − u_2 = U_2, u_2 − u_3 = U_5; adding, u_4 − u_3 = U_1 + U_2 + U_5 = −7 V, so u_3 = 7 V.

hints: Branch admittances: Y = diag(1/2, 1/6, 1/3, 1/4, 1/2, 0, 1/4) S (a current-source branch has admittance 0); signs of U_s1 = 12 V and I_s6 = 2 A per the standard-branch convention.
Y_t can be read off: diagonal = sum of the admittances in the cut-set; off-diagonal = admittances shared by two cut-sets, + if oriented the same way in both, − otherwise.
Once the tree-branch voltages are known, any node voltage follows by adding them along the tree from the reference node.
solution: **Source vectors:** the "+" of branch 1 faces node 1 (its end) → U_s1 = **+12 V**; I_s6 points up (4→3), against branch 6 (3→4) → I_s6 = **+2 A**.
**Check (KCL at node 3):** I_s6 brings in 2 A; R_5 brings (6.5 − 7)/2 = −0.25 A; R_7 takes 7/4 = 1.75 A out: 2 − 0.25 = 1.75 ✓.
